answer: An AI agent economy can achieve robust Sybil resistance by anchoring identity to a cryptographic compute-stake vault where execution traces are verified on-chain. To harbor legitimate agents without centralized gatekeepers, the network evaluates historical task success against a dynamic economic threshold. An attacker attempting to flood the system must acquire massive computational resources and lock up capital, making identity falsification economically irrational because the capital cost scales linearly with the number of simulated identities deployed across the mesa.
